report.finding:
There is no steady state for this parameter set, so nleq2 (or any solver) cannot converge. J2's rate law is substrate-inhibited and therefore bounded: max(Vm*S1/(Km+S1+S1²/Ki)) over S1≥0 occurs at S1=sqrt(Km*Ki)=0.0707, giving a maximum possible efflux of only ≈2.61. The constant influx vo=4.5 exceeds this ceiling, so S1 can never be drained fast enough — it grows without bound, exactly as seen in the time course (S1 rising past 800 by t=200 with no sign of leveling, while S2 decays toward ~0 because J2's rate is already saturated/falling on the far side of the inhibition peak). The Jacobian is singular because nleq2's iterate is being pulled toward the point of maximum J2 flux (S1≈0.0707), which is not a fixed point, just the best the sink can ever do - not a genuine root of the flux-balance equations.

This is not a numerical/solver issue: allow_presimulation fails for the same reason (presimulating just runs the same unbounded trajectory). Switching integrators or solvers won't help because no root exists mathematically.</finding>

Time course confirms: S1 climbs monotonically to ~899 by t=200 with no plateau; S2 decays to ~0.00056, i.e. J2's rate has fallen well below vo as S1 leaves the inhibition peak, so the imbalance only worsens with time.</parameter>
